summary: Guidance + safe-toggle script for reconciling mixed batching/quant profiles causing burst tail-latency
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 95th/99th tail latency spikes (up to +600ms) on text-generation routes after a recent optimizer rollout that applied combined batching caps and a new mixed quant profile. Impact: Production traffic for ParagraphAI (dedicated) experiences request timeouts and degraded UX during bursty traffic windows. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 running serving-runtime v2.18 with autoscaler enabled and latest optimizer controller applied on 2026-03-12 22:18 UTC. Observed behavior: increased token-latency variance, occasional 504s for streaming clients, and elevated GPU mem churn on pool-03 nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target the customer route /v1/generate with typical payloads (avg 350 tokens) and parallelism of 20 connections from us-east test harness.
2) Apply mixed-quant profile + batch cap (batched_max=64, stream_threshold=32) as in their rollout config.
3) Ramp to a 2x baseline QPS over 5 minutes to simulate burst. Observe 95/99 latency and backend 5xx counters in logs and Grafana.
4) Note KV cache hit-rate drop and sporadic model-worker restarts in the same timeframe.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: latency increase correlates with rollout timestamp; canary pods showed no issues but dedicated pool experienced cross-tenant memory pressure.
Hypothesis A: mixed-quant profile increased per-token CPU/GEMM working set causing more frequent KV cache evictions under heavy batching, increasing cache-miss penalty.
Hypothesis B: batch cap misconfiguration allowed oversized batches to queue on a small subset of workers leading to tail amplification during bursts.

Observed: KV cache hit-rate fell from 98% to 72% at spike, and p99 tokenize time rose by ~420ms on pool-03. No disk OOMs, but worker restarts correlate with transient CUDA OOMs logged immediately prior to 504s.
temporary_workaround: We advised customer to pin traffic to the previous optimizer profile via route override (console -> route config -> use snapshot <snapshot-id>) and to temporarily reduce client concurrency from 20 -> 8. This reduced p99 by ~300ms immediately.
recommended_safe_rollback_plan: 1) Validation: run dry-run validator script (see related_github_prs) against current config to detect mismatched quant/batch rules and invalid batch caps. 2) Toggle: use the /admin/v1/toggles endpoint to flip optimizer.enable_mixed_quant to false for the affected tenant on prod-us-east. 3) Staged revert: apply previous optimizer snapshot (snapshot-2026-03-11-2130) to one availability zone pool and monitor 10 minutes. 4) Full revert: if metrics stabilize, roll snapshot to remaining pools during low-traffic window; keep autoscaler conservative for 30 minutes. 5) Post-mortem: capture full traces, KV cache metrics, and create a follow-up INT ticket for root cause analysis.
safe_toggle_script: # After toggle: run validator: python tools/opt_validator.py --tenant $TENANT --dry-run --cluster prod-us-east
validator_output_summary: Dry-run validator detects: one route with batch_cap 1024 (exceeds supported soft-limit for the pool), quant-profile mix flagged for redwood/open-7b-ql. Suggested action: reduce batch_cap to 128 and disable mixed quant for tenant until per-worker mem use is validated.
next_steps: 1) Engineering POC: Diego to run staged revert on pool-03 at 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC and monitor p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit-rate, and CUDA OOM events.
2) CS: Notify ParagraphAI of planned revert window and recommended client concurrency reduction during the maintenance window.
3) SRE: Keep autoscaler headroom +10% during revert to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts.
4) Follow-up INT ticket: capture heap profiles and quant kernel metrics for deep analysis (create INT-XXXX).
